Organize your projects, work with Codex: Organize your projects, work with Codex agents and keep track of shared knowledge, actions and deliverables. This guide explains where to start and how the features fit together.
Create a project from the + beside Proje: Create a project from the + beside Projects and choose its name.
Add shared instructions and attach any s: Add shared instructions and attach any secondary workspaces you need in the project settings.
Use the project + menu to start a conver: Use the project + menu to start a conversation or add the managers you need.
Give the agent a clear goal, follow its: Give the agent a clear goal, follow its work, then review the result and keep useful decisions in shared knowledge.
A project brings together conversations,: A project brings together conversations, workspaces, shared knowledge and optional managers. Use its + menu to create a work agent, a simple conversation, a task manager, an automation manager or a deliverables manager.
Home gives you an overview of projects,: Home gives you an overview of projects, upcoming deadlines and actions that need attention. Open a project to manage its participants, settings and resources.
Use a simple conversation to ask questio: Use a simple conversation to ask questions and discuss ideas. A work agent can inspect and modify files and run commands with the tools and permissions available to it. Describe your goal, the expected result and any constraints.
Each conversation has its own history. S: Each conversation has its own history. Shared project knowledge supplies common context to subsequent messages. Follow the conversation status and respond when the agent requests a decision or approval.
Every project has a permanent primary wo: Every project has a permanent primary workspace identified by the project ID. Renaming the project keeps this directory. The primary workspace can only be removed when the project itself is deleted.
Secondary workspaces attach other workin: Secondary workspaces attach other working directories to the project. The active workspace is the directory used by a conversation; it can be primary or secondary. User files and the reserved .webui system directory have separate purposes.
Use the project knowledge tab to manage: Use the project knowledge tab to manage common instructions, useful facts and decisions. These documents live in the primary workspace and provide shared context to conversations in the project.
Important information discussed in a con: Important information discussed in a conversation is not automatically established as project knowledge. Review memory proposals and accept useful changes, or edit the shared documents directly when your role permits it.
Add a task manager when the project need: Add a task manager when the project needs action tracking. Create tasks and subtasks, assign participants, set deadlines and estimates, and follow progress through the board and planning views.
Agent assistance helps carry out work li: Agent assistance helps carry out work linked to a task. Review the result and its validation criteria before marking the action complete. A project can contain several task managers.
A project can add one automation manager: A project can add one automation manager containing several automations. Once it exists, choosing Automations again in the + menu opens that manager.
Configure what each automation should do: Configure what each automation should do, its target and its manual or scheduled execution. Check its run history and results. Server execution and automation management require administrator access.
Add the optional deliverables manager wh: Add the optional deliverables manager when the project needs identifiable outputs. Each record describes the expected result, responsible person, deadline and validation criteria, and can link tasks and conversations. There is one manager per project.
Working files live in the primary worksp: Working files live in the primary workspace. Submitting a version creates a separate copy for review. Explicit validation sets the reference version; preparing the next version preserves it. Removing a record or manager preserves the physical files.
Available actions depend on your role. A: Available actions depend on your role. Administrators manage platform settings, integrations and server execution. Standard users use the features allowed by their account; project participation also lets you assign work to the right person.
Project settings enable or disable avail: Project settings enable or disable available apps and MCP servers for that project. Platform Codex settings configure the server defaults, model behaviour and CLI maintenance. Ask an administrator if a feature is unavailable.
Passwords are hashed with Argon2id and n: Passwords are hashed with Argon2id and never stored in the configuration file.
This person is linked to SSO. A local pa: This person is linked to SSO. A local password cannot be configured.
New password (leave empty to keep it): New password (leave empty to keep it)
Configure at least one active local acco: Configure at least one active local account before enabling local authentication
Disable local authentication before remo: Disable local authentication before removing its last account
A local password cannot be configured fo: A local password cannot be configured for an SSO-linked account
Password must contain at least 12 charac: Password must contain at least 12 characters
Username must contain 3 to 64 lowercase: Username must contain 3 to 64 lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores
